newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to deal appropriately with forex moves - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan to deal appropriately with forex moves - MOF.

text.p: Japan will deal appropriately and in a timely manner with excessive foreign exchange moves, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Tuesday.
"An excessively strong yen or an excessively weak yen is undesirable. We must deal with this in a timely and appropriate manner," he said.
Mitsuzuka said he had instructed ministry officials to keep watch over currency movements and to analyse the reasons behind the currency fluctuations.
"I think the currency moves have been excessive in a short period of time," he said.

Asked about Japan's rising trade surplus, Mitsuzuka said the Group of Seven (G7) industrialised nations had agreed at the April G7 meeting in Washington to cooperate to achieve stable economic growth for each country.
"Domestic demand (in Japan) is steadily expanding," he said.
Mitsuzuka also said: "The trade surplus issue is a temporary one. I have been saying that since the Washington G7 meeting."
Japan will also explain about its economic management and its trade surplus at the G7 meeting in Denver and at bilateral talks with U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin at the meeting, he said.
Asked whether the currency rate is likely to stay at around 112 yen to the dollar until the summit, which will take place on June 20-22, he said that this was difficult to tell.

He said the G7 nations will discuss the currency issue in a situation where some people feel that the dollar/yen is at an appropriate level. Mitsuzuka said that the ministers would also be discussing currencies in a situation where there are fears that the current account surplus is going to increase.
